section_summary: This section contains the title page, table of contents, and opening sections of the monthly political report prepared by the American Embassy in Tokyo for October 1933. It reviews Japan's relations with the United States under newly appointed Foreign Minister Kōki Hirota, public reception of the pending U.S. recognition of the Soviet Union, and internal debates regarding the London Naval Treaty. Furthermore, it surveys Japan's regional and international diplomacy, including Sino-Japanese relations, Indo-Japanese cotton quota negotiations, Australian wool trade disputes, state-building and industrial monopolies in Manchukuo, the stalled sale of the Chinese Eastern Railway, border tensions with the Soviet Union, and Japanese resentment over German racial classifications.

subfiles.about: Monthly diplomatic and political report on conditions in Japan during October 1933 prepared by the American Embassy in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The American Embassy in Tokyo provides a detailed survey of Japanese internal and foreign affairs during October 1933. The report highlights efforts by Foreign Minister Kōki Hirota to improve American-Japanese relations and manage public reaction to the U.S.-Soviet rapprochement, alongside domestic friction concerning naval limitation treaties. In regional affairs, it documents diplomatic maneuvering with China, negotiations in Delhi over Indian raw cotton and Japanese piece goods quotas, and industrial integration and debt repayment in Manchukuo. Finally, it analyzes tensions with the Soviet Union surrounding the Chinese Eastern Railway and border fortifications, as well as Japanese diplomatic protests against racial discrimination in new German regulations.
subfiles.title: Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of October, 1933
